questions.question: In Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Gives citizens the right to request information from "Public Authorities". Information must be provided within 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty involved). Exemptions..."?
questions.explanation: Right to Information (RTI) 2005: Gives citizens the right to request information from "Public Authorities". Information must be provided within 30 days (48 hours if life/liberty involved). Exemptions (Section 8): Sovereignty, security, strategic interests, intelligence agencies. Central Information Commission (CIC) is the appellate body.

questions.question: In Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Lokpal (Union) + Lokayukta (State). Anti-corruption ombudsman. Jurisdiction : PM, Ministers, MPs, Group A/B/C/D officers. Selection Committee : PM (Chair)..."?
questions.explanation: Lokpal & Lokayuktas (2013): Lokpal (Union) + Lokayukta (State). Anti-corruption ombudsman. Jurisdiction : PM, Ministers, MPs, Group A/B/C/D officers. Selection Committee : PM (Chair), Speaker of LS, Leader of Opposition in LS, CJI (or nominee), and an eminent jurist.

questions.question: In Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Established 1964 (Santhanam Committee), statutory status in 2003. "Watchdog of integrity" in govt. Advisory body. CVC appointed by President on recommendation of PM..."?
questions.explanation: Central Vigilance Commission (CVC): Established 1964 (Santhanam Committee), statutory status in 2003. "Watchdog of integrity" in govt. Advisory body. CVC appointed by President on recommendation of PM, Home Minister, and LoP in LS.

questions.question: In Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Statutory body (PHRA 1993). Investigates violations of human rights. "Toothless Tiger" (advisory powers only). Chairman : Retired CJI or Judge of SC. Selection..."?
questions.explanation: National Human Rights Commission (NHRC): Statutory body (PHRA 1993). Investigates violations of human rights. "Toothless Tiger" (advisory powers only). Chairman : Retired CJI or Judge of SC. Selection : PM, Speaker, Deputy Chairman of RS, Home Minister, and LoP in both Houses.

questions.question: In Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC, this exam clue belongs to which area: "Constitutional: Mentioned in Constitution (ECI, CAG, UPSC). Statutory : Created by Act of Parliament (RTI, Lokpal, CVC, NHRC). Executive : Created by Cabinet..."?
questions.explanation: Statutory vs Constitutional vs Executive: Constitutional: Mentioned in Constitution (ECI, CAG, UPSC). Statutory : Created by Act of Parliament (RTI, Lokpal, CVC, NHRC). Executive : Created by Cabinet resolution (NITI Aayog, CBI).

topic_title: Governance Bodies: RTI, Lokpal, CVC & NHRC
lesson_intro: Today we move from the Constitution to 'Governance'. These bodies—some statutory, some executive—are designed to fight corruption and protect human rights. From the Right to Information (RTI) which empowered the common citizen, to the Lokpal which acts as an anti-corruption ombudsman for high officials, these institutions are the watchdogs of our democracy. For a UPSC aspirant, understanding their composition, appointment process (the 'Selection Committees'), and their powers is essential for GS Paper 2.
